object_context: Can the scale-invariant strain-formulation remainder identified by Miller be controlled by the joint effect of exact Navier-Stokes evolution and finite-energy/global localization, rather than by a static energy or local-geometry inequality?
structural_coordinates: 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes on R^3, positive Clay regularity lane with smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free initial data
strain S=nabla_sym u and vorticity omega=curl u; the strain-space projection P_st is nonlocal and order zero
define R=P_st((u·nabla)S+S^2+(3/4)omega⊗omega), the perturbation away from Miller's globally regular strain-vorticity interaction model
Miller's blowup criterion requires limsup ||R||_2/||-Delta S||_2 >= 1 at any finite maximal time for H^3 mild solutions
under true Navier-Stokes scaling u_lambda=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), both ||R||_2 and ||-Delta S||_2 scale as lambda^(5/2), so their ratio is scale invariant
parent A1 rejects energy-only critical control on arbitrary histories; parent A2/A3 rejects local pointwise geometry unless exact evolution and finite-energy localization are used jointly
the Clay energy bound is L_t^infinity L_x^2 plus integrated H^1 dissipation; it does not statically control higher derivatives at t=0

smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free fields are admissible initial data for local smooth Navier-Stokes evolution, so a snapshot inequality claimed from kinetic energy alone must hold on that entire initial-data class

advection is L2-neutral in the strain energy identity but can alter higher derivative/frequency structure; any useful depletion mechanism may therefore need a trajectory or time-integrated formulation
pressure/projection and Biot-Savart couplings remain nonlocal; a pointwise or unprojected cancellation is not automatically a bound on R
equivalent_formulations: derive from finite-energy Navier-Stokes dynamics an eventual bound ||R(t)||_2 <= (1-delta)||-Delta S(t)||_2 with delta>0 before any singular time
find a scale-invariant time-integrated version of Miller's perturbation criterion whose finiteness follows from the energy inequality and exact dynamics
prove that viscosity plus self-advection moves strain into a regime where the projected nonlinear remainder is dissipatively dominated
falsify any proposed snapshot estimate Q(u)=||R(u)||_2/||-Delta S(u)||_2 <= F(||u||_2) on the full smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free initial-data class
solved_analogues: Miller's strain-vorticity interaction model, globally regular for all L2 strain data because its H1 identity closes after the exact strain-vorticity orthogonality
2D incompressible Navier-Stokes, where vortex stretching is absent and enstrophy/dissipation estimates close globally
passive-scalar advection-diffusion in shear flows, where advection can accelerate dissipation by rearranging spatial structure even though advection itself is energy-neutral
near_solved_analogues: Miller 2026 perturbative strain criteria for full 3D Navier-Stokes using the projected advection-plus-quadratic remainder
critical Serrin/strain-eigenvalue conditional regularity criteria that close once an external scale-critical quantity is controlled

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A divergence-free shear can leave the scalar L2 energy pairing unchanged while repeatedly rearranging the scalar so diffusion acts on steeper gradients and dissipates it faster.
common_abstraction: transport is neutral in a coarse energy budget
dissipation acts more strongly after that rearrangement
the useful statement is trajectory-level rather than a snapshot bound from coarse energy
source_to_target_mapping: passive transport -> Navier-Stokes advection of strain
scalar gradient creation -> redistribution of strain derivatives/frequencies
enhanced decay criterion -> time-integrated dominance of viscous strain dissipation over the projected nonlinear remainder
shared_constraints: the proposed target quantity must respect Navier-Stokes scaling
the mechanism must be causal and use actual evolution
coarse L2 energy neutrality alone cannot certify the derivative-level effect
disanalogies: the Navier-Stokes velocity transports and is generated by the same state
strain has quadratic self-amplification and vorticity production terms
P_st and pressure introduce nonlocal singular-integral structure
no prescribed shear or fixed enhanced-dissipation timescale is available
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before searching for a pointwise remainder-smallness theorem, test whether fixed kinetic energy can control Miller's dimensionless remainder ratio at one snapshot; if not, restrict the live analogy to time-integrated or positive-time depletion generated by the equation.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Construct an explicit smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free initial datum with nonzero projected-remainder pairing and apply an energy-preserving spatial concentration. If the normalized remainder ratio has a positive concentration exponent, reject all energy-only snapshot bounds for this coordinate.
